title: Dynamic KV page coalescing and GPU eviction simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a prototype that performs dynamic page coalescing for the paged/blocked KV cache and an in-situ GPU eviction simulator so we can evaluate eviction policies against continuous-batching workloads. Goal is to reduce cross-page fragmentation and unnecessary GPU<->CPU swap churn while preserving 99th percentile latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay request traces and output eviction traces and memory residency timelines
Coalescing policy reduces number of discrete GPU page allocations by >= 25% on medium-length chat traces
End-to-end P99 latency regressions < 5% compared to baseline with same batch size distribution
Memory swap volume reduced by >= 20% for long-context workloads (32k tokens) in synthetic traces
implementation_notes: Prototype uses existing paged kv slab metadata but introduces a 'merge window' heuristic for adjacent pages that are hot within the same batch epoch
Eviction simulator runs as a detached process consuming trace events (token start/end, kv hits/misses, batch boundaries) and models GPU memory residency with coarse time quantization (1ms buckets)

Coalescing done at allocation time: small contiguous blocks marked as candidate-merge; background coalescer consolidates during low-load windows; fallback to split pages if access locality becomes skewed
Eviction scoring uses a compound metric: access recency (LRU-ish), per-token reuse probability (estimated from trace), and merge-cost (estimated CPU/GPU copy cost)
Interface hooks required in runtime: page metadata annotate, background coalescer trigger points, and swap accounting telemetry
tradeoffs: Aggressive coalescing lowers fragmentation but can increase copy overhead when merged pages need to be split; weigh by merge-cost in policy
Simulator simplifies kernel contention and does not model warp-level stalls — good for eviction signal but may under/over-estimate micro-latency effects
Background consolidation requires low-load windows; on sustained high-utilization the policy should opportunistically defer coalescing to avoid throughput loss
experiments: Experiment A: Replay 10k real-chat traces (mixed short/long) with baseline slab allocator vs dynamic-coalesce; measure allocation count, eviction count, swap bytes
Experiment B: Continuous batching stress: simulate 500 qps with 8-64 batch sizes, measure P50/P95/P99 latency impact when coalescer runs every 5s vs 30s
Experiment C: Prefetch hint evaluation: compare aggressive prefetching of coalesced pages vs on-demand prefetch under GPU memory pressure
preliminary_results: Local simulator run (sample trace set): allocations reduced by 28%, eviction count down 18%, swap bytes down 22%
P99 latency increased by 3.6% in worst-case continuous-batch synthetic (within acceptance threshold)
Background coalescer running too frequently caused 5-7% throughput jitter on heavy kernels — tuned to run on observed idle epochs
risks: Incorrect merge heuristics can amplify copy overhead and increase latency—need conservative rollout and telemetry to detect regression
Simulator fidelity: missing device-level contention modeling could hide micro-SLO violations
Interaction with existing KV sharding policies may reduce effectiveness if coalesced pages span shards
